premises: Phase-selective recrystallization can be achieved in eutectic high-entropy alloys by controlled thermal-mechanical processing.
This treatment eliminates weak boundaries (phase and grain boundaries) that limit ductility.
Eliminating weak boundaries fully releases the strain hardening capacity of both phases.
The resulting microstructure consists of a fully recrystallized soft phase embedded in a retained hard-phase skeleton.
This microstructure simultaneously improves strength (~2 GPa true stress) and ductility (~35% uniform elongation) over the as-cast state.
